description: Learn how to crochet a cozy beginner-friendly cardigan with simple panels, sleeves, a button band, and easy finishing steps.

title: Crochet Baby Blanket
description: A soft, beginner-friendly crochet baby blanket with a simple shell texture, gentle shaping, and a scalloped border.
materials: DK baby yarn, 5.5 mm hook, scissors, tapestry needle
intro: Start with a soft washable yarn and a foundation width that feels useful rather than oversized.
steps: Choose a foundation chain for the desired width.
Work the shell pattern across each row.
Continue until the desired length, then add a scalloped border.
checkpoint: Check the width after every few rows.
troubleshooting: If shells look crowded, loosen tension or use a larger hook.
finishing: Weave in ends and shape the blanket flat if the yarn allows.
variations: Try two neutral shades or a contrasting border.
care: Wash and dry according to the yarn label.

title: Crochet Baby Booties
description: A sweet beginner crochet baby booties tutorial using a small oval sole, shaped upper, toe decreases, and a simple tie.
materials: Soft baby yarn, 3.5 mm hook, tapestry needle, scissors
intro: Baby booties are small, but accurate counting matters.
steps: Build the upper and shape the toe.
Finish the ankle and make the second bootie.
checkpoint: Lay the two soles together before shaping the uppers.
troubleshooting: If the sole curls, check stitch placement around the ends.
finishing: Weave in ends inside the bootie.
variations: Make a matching pair in two colors.
care: Follow the yarn label for washing.

title: Crochet Beanie for Beginners
description: Make a cozy beginner beanie with a simple round crown, even body, and optional pom-pom finish.
materials: Worsted yarn, 6 mm hook, stitch markers, scissors
intro: A beanie is a useful first wearable because small changes in hook size and tension are easy to see.
steps: Start at the crown and increase evenly.
Finish with a firm edge and optional pom-pom.
checkpoint: Measure the crown flat without stretching it.
troubleshooting: If the crown becomes wavy, there are too many increases.
finishing: Weave the tail through several stitches.
variations: Use stripes or a folded brim.
care: Wash according to the yarn label.

title: Crochet Bookmark
description: A slim crochet bookmark with a delicate lace section, tassel, blocking, and gift-ready finishing.
materials: Thin cotton yarn, 3 mm hook, scissors, yarn needle
intro: A bookmark is a great scrap-yarn project.
steps: Chain to the length you want.
Work a narrow lace-style stitch pattern.
Finish with a small tassel and block flat.
checkpoint: Check the length inside a book before finishing.
troubleshooting: If the edges wave, reduce tension changes.
finishing: Trim the tassel evenly and block if the yarn permits.
variations: Try a contrast tassel or a tiny flower.
care: Keep it dry and wash gently if the fiber allows.

title: Crochet Bucket Hat
description: A beginner bucket hat with a rounded crown, straight side depth, widening brim, and optional structured edge.
materials: Bulky cotton yarn, 5.5 mm hook, stitch markers, measuring tape
intro: Cotton is useful for a bucket hat because it gives the fabric enough structure to hold the brim.
steps: Work the side section, then widen the brim.
Finish with a final edge that stabilizes the shape.
checkpoint: Check crown width before adding depth.
troubleshooting: A wavy brim usually means increases were added too quickly.
finishing: Weave in ends and lightly shape if the cotton allows.
variations: Add stripes or a contrast brim.
care: Spot clean or wash according to the yarn label.

title: Crochet Cardigan
description: A beginner-friendly cardigan construction using a back panel, two front panels, simple sleeves, and a button band.
materials: Worsted yarn, 5.5 mm hook, scissors, tapestry needle, buttons
intro: A simple panel construction makes a cardigan easier to adjust.
steps: Make the back panel first, then two front panels.
Add a button band and finish with buttons.
checkpoint: Lay the front panels over the back before seaming.
troubleshooting: If the cardigan pulls at the shoulders, recheck panel width.
finishing: Block panels before assembly when the yarn allows.
variations: Try a cropped length or contrast cuffs.
care: Wash according to the yarn label and store flat.
